_note: Human air traffic control timings used in docs/26 and scripts/task_latency_report.py. kind SOURCED = a published figure; MODELLED = our own arithmetic from stated assumptions; NOT_MEASURED = no figure found, so no comparison is made. Nothing here is a measurement of Unstep's users.

items.task: Pilot starts the readback after the instruction ends
items.source: NASA NTRS 20220007116, Lutz et al. 2022: average pilot readback latency about 0.6 s on recorded controller-pilot voice exchanges

items.task: Notice that a call was stepped on
items.source: FAA CAMI DOT/FAA/AM-05/19 (2005): blocked calls in 1.16 percent of sampled transmissions at the five busiest US TRACONs and no alerting system for stepped-on or clipped transmissions; NTSB hearing 2025 (AIN): tower operations manager asked whether a controller can tell, said "There's nothing."
items.note: Noticed through consequences, not automatically; no study measures how long that takes

items.task: Recover a lost instruction by saying again
items.source: docs/18-benchmark.md: pilot reaction 1.5 s (assumption), the request to say again and the full retransmission at 250 ms per word (assumption), plus 300 ms gaps; median over 157 simulated stepped-on calls
items.note: Only if someone noticed the garble

items.task: Speak a clearance on the radio
items.source: docs/18-benchmark.md assumption of 250 ms per word; the airtime of a spoken instruction is the same for a person and for synthetic speech
items.note: Parity expected: speaking takes as long as the words take to say

items.task: Find the FAA paragraph that governs an instruction
items.note: Controllers work from memory and training; there is nothing to compare against

items.source: EUROCONTROL and FAA material: readback and hearback errors are the most common communication problem and hearback often misses them; no timing found
items.note: A rate problem, not a speed problem
